transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. It is nice to meet you; could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, too. Thank you for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess what brought me in is that I just... I don't really feel like myself anymore. I mean, I'm sure it's nothing too terrible, I don't want to make a big fuss out of it, but I've noticed I barely talk to people lately. I just sort of... go flat and quiet. And at work—I'm a building cleaner—just getting started on my cleaning route lately feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. I just can't seem to get the gears turning. 

I hope that makes sense? Is that... is that the sort of thing you're asking about?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, let me think... I guess it hasn't been forever, I promise. It’s just been slowly building for... maybe about a year and five months? Give or take? 

It kind of started right around the time I had to leave my old apartment and move out of my old neighborhood. I know it probably sounds a little silly to let a move affect me this much—I really should just be rolling with the punches, so I'm sorry if I'm making too big a deal out of it. But I guess that's when I first noticed things getting a little harder to manage. 

Is... is that the kind of timeframe you were looking for? I hope I'm giving you the right information.

During this period of about a year and five months, have there been any stretches of time where you felt completely back to your normal self, or has this feeling of being 'flat and quiet' been present most of the time?

Well, um... I guess I haven't really had any long stretches where I felt totally normal. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining! I still get up and go to work and everything. But... yeah, for most of the time since the move, that heavy feeling—the sadness, the low energy, and just... feeling bad about myself and not caring about things I used to like—it's just kind of always there in the background. 

Even on the days when, um... well, when other things are bothering me more. Like... sometimes I hear things, or I get really worried about cameras and stuff like that. I know that probably sounds strange, I'm sorry. But even when those things are the main thing on my mind, the sadness and the flatness are still underneath it all. 

I hope it's okay that I mentioned the other stuff... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture. Am I answering your question alright?
When you hear these voices or feel worried about the cameras, do those experiences happen only when you are feeling at your lowest, or do they also occur when your mood is a little better?

Um... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but they actually happen even when my mood is doing okay. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart! There was actually this one stretch—maybe for a few weeks?—where I felt like my mood had really lifted a bit. I was getting through my meals fine, and work was going a little smoother. I was really trying my best, I promise. 

But... even during those better weeks, I still... well, I still heard my name being called when I was cleaning the stairwells. And I just couldn't shake the feeling—the absolute certainty, really—that the cameras in the hallways were tracking me. 

I know it sounds so strange that I'd still be dealing with that even when I wasn't feeling as sad. I hope it doesn't make me sound too crazy. Is that... does that help answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
During the times when your mood was feeling more stable, how long would the hearing of voices and the worry about the cameras typically last?

Oh, um... well, like I think I just mentioned a moment ago, it lasted for that whole stretch of several weeks. I hope it's okay that I'm sort of repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm being clear for you. 

During those few weeks when my mood had lifted some—when I was getting through my meals and my work shifts a little better—those other things didn't go away at all. I still heard my name echoing in the stairwell, and I stayed completely convinced that those hallway cameras were being used to track me the entire time. It didn't let up, even though I was feeling less sad. 

I really tried to just put my head down and do a good job at work despite it, I promise. I didn't let it stop me from cleaning. Did I... did I explain that okay? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the exact timeline you need.

Looking back over the entire last year and five months, have there ever been periods lasting at least two weeks where you experienced those voices or worries about the cameras, but did not have any significant feelings of sadness or low energy?

Yes, um... I think that's exactly what happened during that stretch I was just talking about. I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make absolutely sure I'm giving you the right answer. 

But yes, for those several weeks—which was definitely longer than two weeks—the sadness really wasn't weighing on me. My mood had lifted, and I was getting through my meals and my cleaning shifts a lot better. I was doing pretty well, honestly! But... yeah, even without the sadness or the low energy, I still heard my name echoing in the stairwells, and I stayed completely convinced that the hallway cameras were being used to track me. 

I hope I'm understanding your question correctly... is that the kind of timeframe you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
